01 / Applied AI · Internship

Scribsy

I built the audio transcription, structured SOAP generation, and note-management workflow for a clinical documentation application.

Software Engineering Intern · N-of-1 AI
June — August 2025

Next.js interface · FastAPI backend

  1. Audio
  2. Transcript
  3. SOAP draft
  4. Review

The problem

Turn a recorded conversation into an organized draft that a practitioner can inspect and edit.

My contribution

Connected audio processing, structured note generation, and a Next.js review interface through FastAPI endpoints.

Key engineering decision

Make the generated note a reviewable draft.

Keep the transcript and structured SOAP sections available in the review workflow, so the practitioner can check and revise the output before exporting it.

Architecture & implementation +
Structure
Whisper transcription feeds a separate summarization service. The response separates subjective, objective, assessment, and plan fields instead of returning an unstructured paragraph.
API behavior
The backend separates upload endpoints, transcription, summarization, note schemas, and CRUD operations. Invalid audio and processing failures return explicit errors.
Public demonstration
The sample visit uses fictional content. Editing and PDF export can be explored without an account or a live AI request.

DeliveredAn audio-to-note review workflow with editable sections and note management.

Next.js · FastAPI · Whisper · Structured SOAP output

02 / Full-stack systems · Personal project

Narrator

I built manuscript upload, persisted narration jobs, chapter playback, and audiobook downloads, including recovery when a worker stops mid-book.

Full-stack developer · Personal project

Author studio · Persisted narration worker

  1. Upload
  2. SQLite queue
  3. Piper worker
  4. Audio

The problem

Book-length audio generation outlives a browser request. A closed tab or interrupted worker should not erase completed chapters.

My contribution

Built the author workspace, authenticated APIs, SQLite job queue, narration worker, and private audio delivery.

Key engineering decision

Persist the job beyond the HTTP request.

A separate worker claims a renewable lease and saves each completed chapter. A retry reuses that progress, while lease tokens prevent a stale worker from publishing results.

Architecture, tradeoffs & validation +
Recovery
Jobs recover after a 30-second worker lease expires. Repeated crashes stop for an explicit retry; completed chapter audio stays saved.
Tradeoff
SQLite and local files keep a self-hosted deployment simple. The backend needs a persistent shared disk; scaling across machines would require a shared database, object storage, and another queue.
Validation in the repository
The integration suite exercises real audio generation, account ownership, upload limits, idempotency, Range playback, and worker crash recovery.
Inspect the worker ↗

DeliveredResumable chapter generation, seekable playback, and MP3 / chapter ZIP exports.

Next.js · TypeScript · SQLite · Piper · FFmpeg · Docker

Christopher Housholder · Xuantong Ning · Zelun He · Yifan Zhang

I ran Dozerformer ablation experiments to compare the contribution of the encoder and decoder, and coauthored the forecasting research.

Related recognition: 1st place, Computer Science · 2025 CNAS Undergraduate Research Symposium.

Working manuscript · Not peer reviewed

Gene classification

I benchmarked DNABERT against simple DNA sequence features using nested gene-level and similarity-grouped splits, then reported uncertainty in the held-out results.

The short fine-tuning protocol did not establish an advantage over the simple baselines. The manuscript documents the evaluation design and its limits.

PyTorch · DNABERT · Nested cross-validation
